How does Miroir load and manage its client cache today?

Long image

A

Answer

The client keeps one Redux local cache per browser. A refresh loads whole deployments eagerly, reports fill only lazy entities on demand, and writes update the cache in place without a refetch.

  1. A rollback reads every model entity and every data entity whose cache.cacheAllInstancesOnRefresh is not false, one read per entity.1
  2. Only Blob and PageLoadMeasurement opt out today; a report fills them through ReportQueryLoadService, full, projected or by primary key.2
  3. A plain instance write goes to the store first, then the same action is applied to the cache; a transactional write stays in the cache until commit.3
  4. Every cache write replaces the current object, so every memoized query selector recomputes.4

Applies toClient local cache (miroir-localcache-redux) at commit fd3d979 on _integration. Server-side store caches out of scope. Line numbers from that commit. Re-render cost is read from the code, not measured.

1

Which parts hold and move cached data?

Diagram structure
  • React reports ui
  • Memoized selectors sel
  • ReportQueryLoadService loader
  • Client DomainController dc
  • Redux LocalCache cache
  • PersistenceReduxSaga saga
  • REST server server
  • Persistence stores stores
  • ui → sel · select
  • sel → cache · read current
  • ui → loader · ensureLoaded
  • loader → saga · read missing
  • loader → cache · load instances
  • ui → dc · actions
  • dc → saga · store actions
  • dc → cache · cache actions
  • saga → server · HTTP
  • server → stores · read / write
  1. Redux LocalCache ↗

    Holds a loading zone, a current zone and an undo history. Readers only see current.

  2. Memoized selectors ↗

    Run queries synchronously over current. A missing lazy entity reads as an empty index, not an error.

  3. Client DomainController ↗

    Owns full refreshes (rollback), writes and commit. It is the only writer apart from the report loader.

  4. ReportQueryLoadService ↗

    Fetches what a report needs and is missing, then writes it straight into the cache.

  5. REST server ↗

    Answers reads from the stores. Its own LocalCache is never loaded.

Cache key
deploymentUuid_section_entityUuid, plus __partial for projected rows
Sections
model, data, modelVersion, devData
Segment header
full or partial, fresh or stale
Per-entity policy
Entity.cache.cacheAllInstancesOnRefresh, default true
2

What happens on startup or refresh?

Diagram structure
  • Page (usePageConfiguration) page
  • ConfigurationService cfg
  • DomainController dc
  • Persistence store store
  • LocalCache cache
  • page → cfg · fetchMiroirAndAppConfigurations
  • cfg → dc · rollback Admin, then one per deployment
  • dc → store · read Entity list
  • store → dc · Entity rows
  • dc → store · one read per model entity
  • dc → store · one read per eager data entity
  • store → dc · all instances
  • dc → cache · loadNewInstancesInLocalCache
  • dc → cache · rollback: loading replaces current
  • cache → page · new current, selectors rerun
  1. ConfigurationService ↗

    Runs once per SPA lifetime on the first page mount, or again on the AppBar sync button. It loads every deployment listed in Admin.

  2. Persistence store ↗

    Each read is GET /CRUD/{deployment}/{section}/entity/{entity}/all. Model entities are always read in full.

  3. LocalCache ↗

    One action loads every collection into loading and current. The reducer then drops the deployment's keys from current and merges loading.

The refresh is all-or-nothing per deployment. The local rollback also clears the undo history, so it discards uncommitted changes. Switching deployment in the UI triggers no load.5

3

How does a report fill a lazy entity?

Diagram structure
  • ReportViewWithEditor rv
  • Selectors sel
  • ReportQueryLoadService svc
  • REST server srv
  • LocalCache cache
  • rv → sel · useQueryTemplateResults
  • sel → cache · read current
  • cache → sel · empty index for lazy entity
  • rv → svc · ensureLoaded(fingerprint)
  • svc → cache · segment sufficient?
  • cache → svc · missing or stale
  • svc → srv · one read per target
  • srv → svc · instances
  • svc → cache · loadNewInstancesInLocalCache
  • cache → sel · new current, recompute
  • sel → rv · rows
  1. ReportQueryLoadService ↗

    Keys each request by a fingerprint of report, query, params and projection. One request per key runs at a time.

  2. LocalCache ↗

    A fresh segment of the right kind, and the row for a primary-key target, makes the load a no-op.

  3. REST server ↗

    Instance-list targets use a full or projected read. Primary-key targets run a storage query merged into the segment.

  4. Selectors ↗

    The loader writes the cache directly, with no rollback, so the report re-renders from the selector.

External extractors bypass the cache

A query on an external data source runs on the server with the storage strategy. Its result is kept in the service's per-fingerprint map, not in the cache.

4

What happens to the cache on a write?

Diagram structure
  • UI action act
  • Transactional? tx
  • Write store first wstore
  • Apply to current apply
  • Replay to store replay
  • Apply with undo patch patch
  • Commit commit
  • Clear undo history clear
  • act → tx
  • commit → replay
  • patch → commit · auto or manual
  • replay → clear
  • tx → patch · yes
  • tx → wstore · no
  • wstore → apply · ok
WriteStoreCacheUndo history
createInstance, updateInstance, deleteInstanceWritten firstSame action applied to current after successNot recorded
transactionalInstanceAction (model edits from the UI)Not touched until commitApplied at oncePatch recorded
commitReplays the recorded actionsUnchangedCleared
rollbackRead againDeployment replacedCleared

Neither path refetches after the write. UI actions flagged autocommitFromUI are committed at once, so model edits from the UI reach the store without a manual commit.6 Writes from another client or process never reach this cache until the next full refresh.

5

When is the cache read, and what re-renders?

queryExecutionStrategyBehaviour on the clientStatus
localCacheOrFailRuns over the cache DomainStateImplementedDefault
storageRuns on the server over the storesImplementedUsed by loaders and services
localCacheOrFetchWould read the cache, then fetch on a missThrows
ServerCacheWould use a server-side cacheThrows

The two unimplemented strategies are already declared in the schema, so they are a natural extension point.7

Reports read through createSelector selectors whose first input is the whole current object. Any cache write therefore recomputes every mounted query selector, and a new result object re-renders its component.4 No cache keyed by query exists; the queriesResultsCache field is reset on each action but has no reader. ReportSectionListDisplay also creates a new selector map on every render, so its memoization never hits.8

6

Where are the gaps for the target evolutions?

GoalTodayGap
Load only the needed dataPer-entity opt-out, eager by default. Model always full. Every deployment loaded at startup.{caution:Coarse} No per-page or per-query scope at startup; reads fetch /all without filter or paging.
Refresh only when neededOwn writes patch the cache in place. Full refresh only on startup, the sync button or a runner rollback.{bad:Blind} No staleness signal for other clients' writes. A refresh drops the deployment's report-loaded segments, which then load again.
Smooth UXReport shows a loading message per fingerprint. Sync selectors stay quiet for lazy entities.{caution:Re-renders} Any cache write recomputes all selectors. A failed load stays failed for its fingerprint, without retry.
Server reuseServer LocalCache exists but is never loaded. ServerModelEnvironments caches models and forgets them on writes.{caution:Unused} ServerCache strategy throws; no shared server-side instance cache.9

Points to check before building on this

The rollback reducer merges the whole loading zone, for all deployments, then empties it. Startup runs one rollback per deployment in parallel. This is safe only while each deployment's load and rollback run back-to-back; it is not covered by a test. UndoRedoReducer handles commit itself and never calls the slice's commit branch, so that branch is dead under Redux. A comment in saveInstanceFromUI.ts says the user commits model changes, but autocommitFromUI commits them at once.
